title: Engine texture-view binding requests and native model/context lifetime
status: Static producer, consumer, model setup and teardown evidence. Not a callable UI API or gameplay-verified injection path.

scope: Native engine UI texture-view path using Cohtml. This is not the CRML overlay, nor proof of arbitrary main-menu or HUD page insertion.

binding_request.field_boundary: Wrapper references keyName, modelName, transformID and type. Complete string-field correspondence and all value tags remain to be decoded.
binding_request.ownership: Producer deep-copies strings with 0x318edf0 through typed copy constructors. Enqueue moves the owning variant into a node; temporary destruction is required.

queue.scheduling: Registered dispatcher 0x1b55f60 derives the worker-local command buffer using engine worker index, stride0x1b8 and world+0x585e8.
queue.completion: Consumer unlinks, destroys and frees a request only when variant handler returns true. It otherwise remains pending.
queue.unavailable_target: Tag8 handler returns true even when the target view is absent. Request removal therefore does not prove that bindings were applied.

view_context.binding_assignment: Tag8 resolves the numeric view ID and assigns all three context arrays with typed vector-assignment helpers. This replaces the prior array contents; it does not append an independent mod-owned namespace.
setup_steps: Resolve the native middleware view through 0x34429c0.
Reset binding-manager containers and associate the native view using 0x17e6eb0.
Acquire UI resource with 0x31cab80 and apply resource descriptor spans through 0x17e52d0.
Apply context custom descriptor spans through the same 0x17e52d0.
view_context.setup_boundary: The two no-op helpers are retained in the call graph but must not be advertised as useful setters. Assigning context arrays alone has not established when an already-initialized view rebuilds models.

observations: Ordinary records first decode type and inline/string data into a tagged value. Failed decoding skips insertion.
Insertion requires a non-null middleware view at binding-manager+0x80.
The first string argument is converted to a 64-bit key using 0x32d27b0.
An existing key in the manager tree causes early return instead of overwrite.
Accepted entries construct an owned model value via 0x17da250 and copy it into a 0xf8-byte tree node.
The context constructor owns a built-in world-to-screen transform adapter; arbitrary Wasm callback pointers cannot substitute for this native adapter ABI.
unresolved: which string is the unique namespace key

view_removal: A removal request marks registry record state2.
Advance state2 invokes 0x3482bc0, virtual context destruction, frees the allocation, nulls record+0x18 and writes state3.
Cleanup scans state3 records, destroys owned record string data and compacts the array.

reset_binding_request.target: GlobalID rather than the numeric texture-view ID
reset_binding_request.effect: Resolve GlobalID via0x3f4cd0, validate entity generation/capacity, and append command-buffer removal of component hash0xc5ae4bd3 using0x1b56ac0.
reset_binding_request.boundary: This is an entity structural operation. It is not evidence of an immediate per-mod model clear or whole view destruction.

cleanup.callback_boundary: Owned containers and native context teardown are traced. Cohtml event-handler release acknowledgement, in-flight event callbacks and unload races remain unresolved.

bridge_requirements: Use a dedicated mod-owned native view/context; replacing a shared view binding array would overwrite other bindings.
Expose bounded guest-owned text/value/model descriptions and stable event tokens, never native strings, arrays, vtables or callback pointers.
Create model names and registry ownership under a namespace; handle duplicates explicitly.
Submit work only at the engine UI scheduler boundary; maintain private ownership until completion or rejection.
Observe DOM/script-context readiness and establish when custom binding arrays become active.
Route events to bounded owner-scoped queues and revoke tokens before teardown.
Prove event unregistration, context replacement, reload and pending-request cancellation before Wasm exposure.
